result.text: Title: Luxury Airplane You produce airplanes.
While the base model is always the same, your customer likes to pimp their airplane with fancy interior.
You let them decide between a number of 5 different bars, the number of seats, their color, and the amount of water in the toilets of their plane (you can come up with additional stuff).
After you received the specifications you send the requirements to different teams to manufacture the parts.
E.g.
manufacturing the vodka bar is done by the Russian team, the whiskey bar is manufactured by an Irish team.
After receiving the individual bits and pieces, the interior of the plane is assembled, and the plane is sent on a test flight.
During the flight you create a test protocol which is sent to you and the customer.
The plane is delivered to the customer, which has to confirm.

args.text: When the description states that independent activities happen in parallel and all must finish before the process continues, model them as branches from a parallel gateway and synchronize them with a parallel gateway before the dependent activity.

trace.reason: Check whether a documented guideline already covers parallel branches and synchronization.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.

args.text: When the description says that work occurs while another activity is in progress, model the work as parallel branches and synchronize them before continuing if both must be complete.

trace.reason: Check whether an already learned guideline covers the concurrent work and synchronization implied by the records.

result.rule: When the description says that one activity can be carried out while another activity or sequence of activities is underway, and that both tracks must be complete before a later activity can proceed: Model the tracks as concurrent branches, using a parallel gateway to split them and a parallel gateway to synchronize them before the dependent activity.

When the description states that an activity is required while another activity may be performed only if a stated condition holds, and that the flow continues after the applicable work is complete: Model the activities as branches from an inclusive split, with the condition on the optional branch, and use an inclusive join to synchronize the branches that were activated before the dependent next step.

When the description states that an activity is followed by a decision, synchronization, or cycle-exit condition, or that concurrent work begins after a preceding activity: Connect the activity to the relevant gateway with a sequence flow; for concurrent work, route the preceding flow through a parallel gateway that starts the concurrent branches.
When the description states that one activity must happen before another: Model the activities with sequence flows in the stated order, not as concurrent branches.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
